title: Newly uploaded videos intermittently fail playback
description: Starting around 18:05 UTC on 16 August 2026, users reported that newly uploaded videos on AcmeStream intermittently fail to play, returning HTTP 503 errors. Videos transcoded prior to 18:05 UTC continue playing normally. Telemetry shows video uploads succeed, but downstream transcoding output manifests are missing.

canonical_ground_truth.initiating_event: Deployment v3.8.0 reduced transcoder temporary workspace size from 50Gi to 8Gi and retained retry files
canonical_ground_truth.root_cause_mechanism: Temporary workspace exhaustion (ENOSPC) during video transcoding caused FFmpeg write failures and missing manifests
downstream_symptoms: transcoding queue depth backlog growing to 980 jobs

evidence.content: upload-service health telemetry: p95 request latency: 380ms, HTTP success rate: 99.98%, active upload streams: 210/300. No network connection timeouts or upload drops detected. upload-service is operating normally.

video-transcoding-service disk metrics: Node-3 disk: 97%, Node-5 disk: 97%, Node-8 disk: 98%. Storage threshold 90% crossed at 18:05 UTC. Transcoding job write errors spiked immediately after threshold breach.

Deployment Event: video-transcoding-service release v3.8.0 deployed at 17:58 UTC. Configuration changes: temporary working directory space reduced from 50Gi to 8Gi. Retry policy updated so temporary FFmpeg working files are retained during retry attempts.

Transcoding Service Operations Runbook:
1. Transcoder node disk usage above 90% requires immediate intervention.
2. ENOSPC error indicates FFmpeg temporary working directory space is exhausted.
3. Emergency Mitigation: Roll back recent deployment and clear temporary workspace.
Historical Incident INC-1988 (Resolved in 2024): Database lock contention caused transcoders to stall. Resolved by increasing database connection pool and adding query index.
